title: Where Did Your $100 Go? #money #inflation
description:
Zorb finds out why the same 100 dollars buys a smaller basket of snacks: inflation, a rise in prices across the whole economy. Earth's central bank even aims for a little of it on purpose. Figures: the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (its 100-to-107 dollar example and the CPI for the 12 months ending September 2026) and the Federal Reserve's 2 percent goal, which it measures with a different price index (PCE).

Education, not financial advice.

#Shorts #inflation #personalfinance
pinned_comment: What got more expensive for you this year?

beats.line: Your 100 dollars lost a bag of snacks. Nobody told you why.
Same basket of snacks. Now it costs 107 dollars.
Your 100 dollars did not change. The price did.
That jump is 7 percent. Earthlings call it inflation.
Not just snacks. Prices across the whole economy rise.
Earth's price meter, the CPI, rose in the last 12 months.
So the same money buys a little less.
Twist: Earth's central bank wants some inflation. On purpose.
Its goal is 2 percent a year. Not zero. Two.
